title: James Butler, 1st Duke of Ormond, to his son the Earl of Arran, 24 January 1677/8: twenty code figures set as 'a trial whether you are skilful in deciphering' (HMC Ormonde n.s. iv p. 93; Unsolved Catalogue 353)

documents.shelfmark: National Library of Ireland, Ormonde MSS (letters 1665-80, MSS 2335-2362; NLI Sources MS UR 006261), volume and folio not identified; printed in HMC, Calendar of the MSS of the Marquess of Ormonde, New Series iv (1906), p. 93
documents.route: Ormond, Lord Lieutenant (Dublin) -> his son Richard Butler, Earl of Arran (London)

plaintext.source: HMC prints the figures without a gloss; the manuscript has not been seen. Values come from Tomokiyo's 1680 key shifted by +7 (identification/).

transcription.notes: Figures as printed in HMC n.s. iv p. 93, checked against the Internet Archive scan (calendarofmanusc04greauoft, leaf n122). The sixth figure of the first run is printed 58, not 57 as in Tomokiyo's quotation.

system.summary: Numeric code of the Restoration English type: the Ormond-Longford Cipher 1 (1680) table as reconstructed by Tomokiyo, with every number 7 higher (two regular alphabets 30-53 and 54-77, then syllables and words in alphabetical order). Identified 13 Nov 2026 (identification/).
system.notes: The +7 relation is shown for the entries touched (1680 numbers 25-51, 84-86, 207, 377, 418, 433, 519, 566, 636, 725); whether it holds over the whole table is not known.

prior_solution.where: none found: Cyphersolver ormond1678 (not read; Longford 1 unchanged ruled out), Cryptiana charlesii2.htm (offset 0 trial rejected); Cyphersolver issues, cipher-lab and HMC 6th Report not checked (identification/PRIOR_ART.md)

conditions.human_role: Malcolm McBratney ran an agent on Perplexity that noticed the offset; he set the check task. No other input.
tools: Internet Archive full text and page images
NLI Sources catalogue and collection list A017 (built-in browser)
archive.org page images of HMC Ormonde n.s. V-VII

solution.what: IA full text of HMC Ormonde n.s. iv-v fetched and searched; the passage is the only run of cipher figures in vol. iv; no gloss printed.
p. 93 scan checked: 20 figures; the sixth of run 1 is 58, correcting the 57 in Tomokiyo's quotation and the catalogue.
Ormond-Arran code of 1678 (Arran to Ormond 9 Feb 1677/8, HMC n.s. iv pp. 105-106, with Ormond's interlinear equivalents) examined: a two-letter code (hm, dk, io, yn.xo...), not numeric.

Ormond-Longford 1680 key structure (Tomokiyo's reconstruction from HMC n.s. v pp. 454 ff.; letter slots checked on vol. v p. 498) applied: the low figures 32 33 54 55 58 fall on k l h i m and give consonant runs between alphabetical neighbours, no English. Agrees with Tomokiyo's rejected trial.

Manuscript sought: NLI Sources MS UR 006261 (Ormond to Arran, Jan 7, 24 ... 1678, Ormonde MSS); NLI list A017 puts the 1665-80 letters in MSS 2335-2362. Volume and folio not identified; not digitised.
20 figures, 20 distinct, range 32-732: no repeats to anchor a ciphertext-only solver; no solver run, since a same-length control in a code of this size cannot succeed.

Tomokiyo's Ormond-Longford Cipher 1 (1680) applied with every 1678 figure reduced by 7: run 2 reads 'to Ormond not c-re-di-b-le', run 1 'an-d King ar-e in a'. Offsets -150..+150 on Longford 1 and 2 (602 trials) and Longford 3.

Every 1680 value used checked on the page images of HMC n.s. V pp.454, 469, 479, 486, 498 (identification/GLOSS_CHECK.md); 566 = Ormond rests on the plain rendering on p.498 and the gloss 'Dor' on p.454; 418 = King is context only.

Longest vocabulary word over 3+ groups: only -7 of 301 offsets on K1 gives one ('credible'); 2,000 random figure sets at their best of 602 key-offset pairs reach 8+ letters 6/2000; 3,000 shuffles at -7 reach 8+ letters 0/3000 (identification/controls_out.txt).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's reconstruction of the 1680 Ormond-Longford key, from the HMC n.s. V glosses, read the 1678 figures once each is reduced by 7.

gaps.detail: no gloss for these numbers in HMC n.s. V; MS. Carte 50 fols 439-440 and the NLI letter not seen

gaps.item: gloss on the sent letter or Ormond's copy
